Wave.name: IncrementalStreamingArchitecture
Wave.goal: Reduce perceived latency by overlapping STT, translation, queue control, and playback on stable partials rather than full-utterance boundaries.

ExecutionOrder.step-1: W3-C1 incremental STT first, because partial and stable-partial events are the prerequisite signal for all downstream incremental work.
ExecutionOrder.step-2: W3-C2 segmenter and queueing second, because stable partials need bounded downstream control before early playback is enabled.
ExecutionOrder.step-3: W3-C3 incremental TTS last, because early playback should be layered on top of already-stabilized transcript and queue semantics.

Change.summary: Emit partial and stable-partial transcript events from the STT layer while preserving current final transcript compatibility.

implementation-tasks.task-1: Extend the STT event flow to emit `PARTIAL` and `STABLE_PARTIAL` markers before `FINAL` for the same utterance.
implementation-tasks.task-2: Carry the new event types through the Rust engine and Elixir event routing without breaking the existing final-transcript path.
implementation-tasks.task-3: Update pipeline state and UI handling so partials can be displayed or tracked distinctly from final transcripts.

verification-step.runtime-check: Run long-phrase tests and confirm `[STT] PARTIAL`, `[STT] STABLE_PARTIAL`, and `[STT] FINAL` markers appear in sequence.

done-when.item: Stable partials reach the UI before final transcript completion.
Final transcripts remain backward-compatible with the current event flow.
`pipeline_trace.log` shows `PARTIAL`, `STABLE_PARTIAL`, and `FINAL` markers for incremental runs.

stop-if.item: Partial event emission breaks the current final transcript contract.
UI or pipeline state becomes ambiguous between live and final transcript ownership.

Change.summary: Add text stabilization and stale-job cancellation so repeated prefixes are not retranslated or replayed unnecessarily.

implementation-tasks.task-1: Introduce a segmenter that identifies confirmed stable text boundaries suitable for downstream translation and playback.
implementation-tasks.task-2: Introduce queue control that coalesces updates and cancels or drops stale translation and TTS jobs.
implementation-tasks.task-3: Emit explicit runtime markers when stale work is canceled or dropped so queue behavior is visible during verification.

verification-step.runtime-check: Run repeated long-phrase tests and confirm stable prefixes are not translated repeatedly and stale jobs are explicitly reported.

done-when.item: Repeated partial prefixes are not retranslated unnecessarily.
Stale translation and TTS jobs are canceled or dropped with explicit log markers.
`queue_drop_count` can be inferred from runtime evidence.

stop-if.item: Queue control silently drops essential work with no audit trail.
Segment stabilization causes duplicated translation output or lost confirmed text.

Change.summary: Allow early playback from confirmed translated segments instead of waiting for full utterance completion.

implementation-tasks.task-1: Introduce a scheduler or equivalent control path that can queue early audio from confirmed translated segments.
implementation-tasks.task-2: Measure and emit `time_to_first_audio_ms` independently from full-utterance `total_ms`.
implementation-tasks.task-3: Ensure incremental playback does not duplicate or replay already-confirmed audio when later text arrives.

verification-step.runtime-check: Run long-phrase tests and confirm playback starts before full-utterance completion while avoiding duplicated output.

done-when.item: `time_to_first_audio_ms` is logged and measured separately from total utterance time.
Users hear the beginning of the translation before the source speaker finishes long sentences.
Runtime logs support verification that early playback preceded final transcript completion.

stop-if.item: Incremental playback introduces duplicated or out-of-order translated audio.
Early playback hides failures that should remain observable in runtime evidence.

acceptance-targets.item: Stable partial appears meaningfully earlier than final transcript on long phrases.
Playback begins before full-utterance completion on long phrases.
Stale jobs are controlled explicitly rather than accumulating invisible backlog.
